name: Hagabah
overview: Hagabah was a male member of the tribe of Levi, serving as a temple servant. His role as a temple servant highlights his participation in the religious functions and duties associated with the Levitical priesthood during the post-exilic period. Scripture identifies him specifically in the context of temple service without additional personal details.
namesAndTitles: The name Hagabah, also spelled Hagaba, means 'locust' in Hebrew. This proper name does not appear to have been given directly by God but reflects a common Semitic naming practice. The name's meaning, while noted, does not carry explicit theological significance in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Hagabah as a descendant of Levi, indicating his Levitical lineage essential for temple service. Beyond this tribal affiliation, no other family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Hagabah's significance lies in his role as a temple servant from the tribe of Levi during the return from exile, as recorded in Ezra 2:45 and Nehemiah 7:48. His inclusion in the genealogical lists underscores the restoration of proper worship and the reestablishment of Levitical duties in Jerusalem. Though not a prominent figure individually, his presence reflects the faithfulness of God's people in resuming covenantal worship under Christ-centered redemption.
